precepts.text: Hear, O ye kings, and understand; for power is given you of the Lord and sovereignty from the highest, who shall try your works and search out your counsels; rulers hold a small power from the Most High until the King comes.
precepts.point: He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God, and he shall be as the light of the morning when the sun riseth, a morning without clouds, as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain. This is how you are a great leader: just in your judgments, in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

precepts.why:
“Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations. For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels.”

In his last words David says, “The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.” Rulers hold a small power from the Most High until the King comes, and the Highest will try their works and search out their counsels. So the one who rules must be just in his judgments, in the fear of the Most High. This is how you are a great leader.

And such a ruler “shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.”

David could say this because “The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.” David was a prophet, the sweet psalmist of Israel, and the book of Psalms are songs of prophecy.

points: These are the last words of David, the son of Jesse, the man raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob and the sweet psalmist of Israel. The spirit of the Lord spoke by him and his word was in David's tongue; this shows David was a prophet, and the book of Psalms are songs of prophecy. The God of Israel, the rock of Israel, spoke to him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God, and he shall be as the light of the morning when the sun riseth, a morning without clouds, as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain. This is how you are a great leader: just in your judgments, in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: Although David's house was not perfect with God, yet the Most High made with him an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure, and this was all his salvation and all his desire. Not all David's sons were right; Absalom was wicked and one son violated their sister Tamar. Yet the Lord still promised that his seed should sit on the throne for ever, because David was a man after the Lord's own heart.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: But the sons of Belial, the sons of the devil, shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands; the man that touches them must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear, and they shall be utterly burned with fire. The wicked must be separated from the righteous.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: These are the names of the mighty men whom David had. Adino the Eznite, chief among the captains, lifted up his spear against eight hundred whom he slew at one time. Israel was next level; Samson slew a thousand with a jawbone, and Adino took out eight hundred in one stand.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: After him Eleazar the son of Dodo defied the Philistines when the men of Israel had gone away; he smote them until his hand was weary and clave unto the sword, so that the Most High wrought a great victory that day, and the people returned only to spoil. Then Shammah the son of Agee stood in the midst of a piece of ground full of lentils when the people fled, defended it, and slew the Philistines, and the Lord wrought a great victory.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: Three of the thirty chief went down to David at the cave of Adullam while the Philistines were in the valley of Rephaim, and the garrison was in Bethlehem. David longed and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem by the gate. The three mighty men, Adino, Eleazar and Shammah, broke through the host of the Philistines, drew the water and brought it to David; these were his personal bodyguards.

David would not drink it but poured it out unto the Lord, saying, Is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? They had to break through the camp, draw water from a well by hand while at least two hundred men pressed at their backs, one drawing while the others held off the enemy, and carry it back without spilling a drop. The Most High has promised our people greater power than that if we endure and repent.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: Abishai the brother of Joab was chief among the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them and had a name among the three, and was their captain, but he attained not unto the first three. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did many acts: he slew two lionlike men of Moab, went down and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow, and slew a goodly Egyptian with the Egyptian's own spear after plucking it out of his hand with a staff.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: Benaiah had a name among the three mighty men and was more honourable than the thirty, but attained not to the first three, and David set him over his guard. The two lionlike men of Moab were dark and strong men in that day, before Greece and the nations mixed into Moab; the scripture calls them lionlike because of the fierce strength they had, the same strength Israel had.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: The rest of the thirty are named: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and the others down to Uriah the Hittite, thirty and seven in all. Some carry names like Zelek the Ammonite and Uriah the Hittite, but this does not mean they were Hamites in David's army; it means they dwelt in those lands after Israel removed the nations from the coasts.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: David had three main mighty men who were next level and served as his personal bodyguards, Abishai who was chief over the thirty and seven, and Benaiah who had a name but was not on the level of the first three. This record shows the valour the Most High put upon Israel.
